scenes.heading: Redshift Distribution & Sort Keys
scenes.narration: In Redshift, how you distribute and sort data across slices is the single biggest factor in query performance.

scenes.heading: Distribution styles
bullets: KEY: rows with the same key value land on the same slice for co-located joins.
ALL: a full copy on every node, ideal for small dimension tables.
EVEN: rows spread round-robin when there is no clear join key.
AUTO: Redshift picks and adjusts the style as the table grows.
scenes.narration: KEY distribution places matching join keys on the same slice, which avoids shuffling data during joins. ALL replicates a small table everywhere so it never needs to move. EVEN spreads rows uniformly, and AUTO lets Redshift choose and evolve the style automatically.

scenes.heading: Why distribution matters for joins
scenes.narration: Suppose two large tables both use customer id as their distribution key. Matching rows already sit on the same slice, so no data has to travel across the network. The join then runs entirely locally on each slice, which is far faster than a broadcast or shuffle.

scenes.heading: Distribution key vs sort key

left.title: Distribution key
points: Decides which slice holds a row

right.title: Sort key
points: Great for time and filter columns

scenes.narration: The distribution key controls placement across slices to make joins fast and keep data balanced. The sort key controls ordering within each slice so range filters can skip irrelevant blocks. Pick the distribution key for your biggest joins and the sort key for your most common filters.

scenes.heading: Choosing keys on a fact table
scenes.code:
CREATE TABLE sales (
  sale_id      BIGINT,
  customer_id  BIGINT,
  sale_date    DATE,
  amount       DECIMAL(12,2)
)
DISTSTYLE KEY
DISTKEY (customer_id)   -- co-locate with customers table
SORTKEY (sale_date);    -- fast range scans by date
scenes.narration: This fact table distributes on customer id so it joins cleanly with the customers table on the same slices. It sorts by sale date, letting date-range queries skip blocks outside the requested window. Together these choices reduce both network movement and disk reads for typical sales queries.

scenes.text: Distribute to co-locate your biggest joins and sort on your most common filter columns to slash scans and shuffles.
scenes.narration: Choose distribution keys to eliminate join shuffles and sort keys to prune scans, and your Redshift queries will fly.
